title.quote: New insights into the genetic etiology of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias

design.quote: We performed a two-stage genome-wide association study

outcomes.name: risk loci
outcomes.quote: We found 75 risk loci, of which 42 were new at the time of analysis.

outcomes.name: genetic risk score associated with the risk of future AD/dementia or progression from mild cognitive impairment to AD/dementia
outcomes.quote: We also built a new genetic risk score associated with the risk of future AD/dementia or progression from mild cognitive impairment to AD/dementia.

primary_endpoint_status.quote: We performed a two-stage genome-wide association study totaling 111,326 clinically diagnosed/‘proxy’ AD cases and 677,663 controls.
primary_endpoint_status.explanation: This is a genome-wide association study, not a clinical trial with a primary efficacy endpoint.

conflicts: H. Hampel is an employee of Eisai. limitations: identification of rare variants with very low frequencies is a major challenge for genetic studies, because available samples with sequencing data in AD are underpowered.
gene–gene and gene–environment interactions have not yet been studied in detail.
GRSs developed with European-ancestry populations are known to be less effective with other ancestries
